FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Drinks and Carbonated Beverages Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Fortified wine is a mixture of alcoholic fermentation of fresh grape juice/must of grapes/concentrated grape juiceh-efined sugar of glucose or fructose syrup and neutral spirit possessing distinctive aroma and taste of grape variety used. The standard was originally issued in 1996. The present revision has been taken up in order to update the standard in the light of current industrial and trade practices. The requirements of various characteristics have been modified. In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, and the Rules framed thereunder; Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977 and State Excise Duty Rules. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these Acts and Rules thereunder, wherever applicable. Fortified wine is an alcoholic fermentation possessing the distinctive colour, aroma and taste of grapes. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is compiled with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 1S2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of specified value in this standard.

This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for fortified wines. 2 REFERENCES
The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions, which through reference in this text, constitute provision of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of appIying the most recent editions of the standards indicated at Annex A.

However, the ethyl alcohol content, its tolerance and method of measurement may vary according to the Rules and Regulations prescribed by the State Excise Authority. 7.2 Fortification a) The fermentation shall either be allowed to proceed to completion followed by addition of alcohol to the desired alcoholic strength, or b) The fermentation shall be arrested at a certain "stage of fermentation followed by addition of alcohol to the desired alcoholic strength. 7.3 Quality of Alcohol for Fortification
The source of alcohol shall be grape spirit or rum spirit

a) Fortified white wine, b) Fortified red wine, and c) Fortified sweetened red/white wines. 4.1.1 Fortified white wines shall be the product obtained from the alcoholic fermentation of fresh grape juice!must of white grapes followed by fortification. 4.1.2 Fortified red wines shall be the product obtained from the alcoholic fermentation of fresh grape juice/ must of red grapes followed by fortification. 4.1.3 Fortified sweetened red/white wines shall be the products of fortified white/red wine (see 4.1.1 or 4.1.2) sweetened with either concentrated grape juice/ musthefined sugar syrup of glucose/fructose syrup. 5 HYGIENIC CONDITIONS Fortified wines shall be manufactured under hygienic conditions (see IS 14348). 6 WATER QUALITY Water conforming to IS 14543 or IS 13428 or IS 10500 with or without demineralization shall be used. 7 REQUIREMENTS

Fortified wines shall be free tlom sediments, suspended matter and any ingredients injurious to health. 7.6 Colour and Additives Fortified wines may conhin permitted food additives including colour as defined by PFA/CODEX/.JECFA. The limits shall be in accordance with EU guidelines. 7.7 Taste and Aroma
~

Fortified wines ,shall possess the characteristic taste and aroma associated with wine. To enhance the characteristic flavour of the product, naturalhatural extracts/nature identical/artificial flavour permitted under PFAIFEMA GRAS may be used. 7.8 Fortified wines shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 1.

8.2 Used bottles shall be permitted, if cleaned in a hygienic way by the manufacturer as per 5.6.1.1 of 1S 14348. 8.3 Inspection of Empty and Filled Containers Containers, both before and after tilling, shall pass for inspection before a brightly illuminated background and be viewed, if necessary, under magnification. Automatic inspection by specially designed units may also be employed. Defective containers or products shall be rejected. 8.4 [n case of Fortified Wines: a) All containers shall be cleaned and sanitized according to 4.1 of IS 5837. b) The containers shall be filled under strictly sanitary conditions as per IS 5837. Bureau

of Indian

Standards

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standard Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
Copyright

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'. This Indian Standard has been developed from Dot: No. FAD 14 (1530).
